title: How to reverse-engineer unknown mobile apps making $50K+ MRR and copy the formula
summary: Greg breaks down apps like Vinyl Snap, Lang Lang Learn and an AI interior designer, explaining why each works and which niches to port the format to. He distills them into a five-box filter and six frameworks: start with a nerve, one job, one high-intent input, an AI-unlocked premium insight, and a dead-simple interface.

principles.text: A $50K MRR app idea checks five boxes: spending group, repeating problem, photo/video input, accuracy matters, bad existing tools.
principles.quote: find a group that one, spends money, two, has a repeating problem, three, uses photos and videos as inputs.

principles.text: Start with a nerve, not a market: a niche with identity, urgency, stakes and repetition is ripe for an AI app.
principles.quote: a niche works when it has an identity, it has, you know, collectors professionals, uh churchgoers. Urgency, I need an answer now.

principles.text: Each winning app does one job brutally well: one job times one obsessed group times one recurring need.
principles.quote: the next 50K MRR app, in my opinion, is one job times one obsessed group times one recurring need.

principles.text: Build around a single high-intent input (photo, address, item, prompt); it converts better and lets AI deliver instant value.
principles.quote: the high-intent inputs usually lead to higher conversion.

principles.text: AI is the engine; the product is the premium insight it unlocks that used to take time and expertise.
principles.quote: what is the premium insight that AI can unlock instantly that used to take time and expertise.

principles.text: Keep the interface brutally simple, and pick a name that wins App Store search since ASO drives discovery.
principles.quote: it's just a simple name, right? Logo Maker. So, it's it's it's sort of relying on ASO, App Store optimization
